articles.title: My mum has died – and there is one kind of response I can’t stand | Polly Hudson
articles.summary: The platitudes, euphemisms and cliches are excruciating. But the people who say nothing at all are the worst. Luckily, I already knew having a comic thought at a tragic moment is a natural stress response, or I might have worried.
body: In Curb Your Enthusiasm, when Marty Funkhouser’s mother’s wheelchair was run over by a car, he proclaimed himself an orphan. David informed him he was too old to be an orphan. Funkhouser insisted that if your parents are dead, you’re an orphan.

Images of Annie-like red curls aside, the people who brought you into the world both having left it is pretty profound. I’m lucky to have a lot of support, but it’s a hard knock in life. A singularly specific brand of aloneness; the natural order that feels anything but. It’s so weird. There’s no one to tell me off any more, either. I wonder what I may get up to. What if I fall in with a bad crowd?

My mum “had a good innings though”, as I have been reminded roughly thrice daily. It’s been 14 years since my dad died, and there’s so much I’d forgotten about the grief game – namely the platitudes, the strange language, and how terrible so many of us are at dealing with it. The best reaction so far was a bloke who replied to my breaking of the news for sadmin purposes with: “OK, that’s fine.” At least he gave me a good story.
points: But the people who say nothing at all are the worst.
Luckily, I already knew having a comic thought at a tragic moment is a natural stress response, or I might have worried.

David informed him he was too old to be an orphan.

articles.title: Stuck bundts? You need ‘cake goop’: Natalie Paull’s lime and yoghurt bundt – recipe
articles.summary: The cookbook author and owner of Melbourne’s Beatrix Bakes shares a her ‘100% reliable’ formula for freeing bundts from tins. When all the layer cakes are baked and iced, I will always love a slice of pretty patterned bundt.
body: Cake goop – a mix of flour, oil and butter – is a gift of guaranteed cake release that I found on the internet, and it means no more stuck bundts. Bless the baker who invented it! Goop has it all – release, plus enough sticking power to hold the batter as it rises and cools, without slumping. Additionally, mixing the flour with oil means you don’t get that fine, white, dusty crust on the outside of the cooked cake. Goop is 100% reliable with a 100% untarnished release record in my kitchen.

If you do have a small stuck piece of cake, shimmy it out of the tin with an offset spatula and patch it back on to the cake while warm. Pretty easy! If a whole ring of cake has stuck, cut it into workable sections, prise each out and place back on the cake. Drench the bundt with icing sugar after its soak to hide the Franken-bundt’s monster appearance.

The recipe calls for the eggs to be warmed before cracking. Warmer-than-room- temperature eggs emulsify into the creamed base better, and an emulsified mix means no “curdled” appearance. To do this, submerge the uncracked eggs in hot tap water for five minutes.

articles.title: Is a $1,000 pillow really better? The expensive pursuit of comfortable sleep
articles.summary: From ergonomic memory foam to luxury goose down, Australia’s options for where to lay your head are enough to make it spin. So how do you choose the perfect pillow? The room inside Hästens’s “sleep spa” is calming.
body: It feels less like shopping and more like checking into a boutique hotel. The luxury brand, which has showrooms in Sydney and Melbourne, has celebrity fans, too. Emily Blunt loves her Hästens pillow so much she gave one to Oppenheimer co-star Cillian Murphy.
But what, exactly, makes a pillow worthy of such devotion? After years hunched over a laptop, plus occasional insomnia and many pillows of my own, I’m hoping to find out.

Sleep specialist Emilia Axelsson watches as I roll on to my side before sliding one pillow from beneath my head and replacing it with another. “This one’s too high,” she says, noticing my chin tip towards my chest. “When a pillow is the wrong height, your muscles work all night to hold your neck in position. The right pillow lets them switch off.”

Based on my fitting, Axelsson recommends two options: the Beddoc Therapeutic Pillow ($1,035), which combines down and feathers with an ergonomic core, and the Hästens High Firm Pillow ($725), a lofty down pillow for side sleepers who need more height.
points: From ergonomic memory foam to luxury goose down, Australia’s options for where to lay your head are enough to make it spin.

articles.title: ‘It was the hardcore equivalent of being a Deadhead’: consciousness-raising punk movement Krishnacore returns
articles.summary: First-wave punks rejected religion – but come the 90s, bands embracing eastern thought found legions of devotees. Ahead of reformations and reissues, they discuss the Bhagavad Gita, brawls and tulasi beads in the pit.
body: Whether wielded as shock tactic or part of a considered philosophical stance, mockery and distrust of religion have been baked into punk rock’s DNA from the get-go. The Damned, Crass, the Germs and the Dead Kennedys all proffered early potshots and takedowns, and if Bad Brains received a grudging pass for their Rastafari leanings, in general, songs kowtowing to gods or masters were about as likely to win you scene cred as praise for Reagan, cops or nuclear war.

As the 80s ticked into the 90s, however, something curious began to happen: a clutch of bands emerged who were wise to the hardcore classicism of Minor Threat and SSD but also looked east to Krishna consciousness. Leading the way was Ray “Raghunath” Cappo who, barely into his 20s, had already broken down walls as frontman for Youth of Today, a New York band who combined a straight-edge philosophy with animal-rights advocacy and a sense of full-throated positivity. He and guitarist John Porcelly had “witnessed enough young people screwing up their lives that we thought, as simple as it is, it’s a positive message. Let’s rally behind it,” he says. “And it became big, bigger than we expected.”
points: First-wave punks rejected religion – but come the 90s, bands embracing eastern thought found legions of devotees.
Ahead of reformations and reissues, they discuss the Bhagavad Gita, brawls and tulasi beads in the pit.

articles.title: I’m Over the Erewhonification of Fancy Grocery Stores
articles.summary: All this week, the Eater Today newsletter is dedicated to editor Hot Takes, a way to release the pressure valve of crankiness that comes with sweating your way through the end of summer. This story was previously published as part of that series.
body: There was a time, long before we’d ever conceived of the phrase “ shoppy shop,” when I loved nothing more than going to a specialty grocery store. “Bougie grocery store” was a phrase I said with love and not an ounce of judgment. I loved the delightfully corny graphic design of the products on shelves at little chef-beloved markets, the rare locations where one could reliably find locally made, small-batch, niche products that weren’t yet available elsewhere.

I went to Eataly when bored, trusting that I’d find something new there to drum up some impulses of desire and inspiration; even if I didn’t buy anything, I could be shaken from the doldrums of daily life by picking up a small piece of obscure cheese, a jar of something I’d never seen in a jar before, or a fancy bag of chips. I loved the curiosity these shelves inspired; they felt like capsules of the world. Here were products I’d never seen at the regular grocery store and which transported me into a vision of a different self — one more learned, more cultured even without traveling, more artistic simply by virtue of having an interesting ingredient to play with.

articles.title: Collagen vs. Collagen Peptides: Which Supplement Is Better?
articles.summary: If you’re comparing collagen vs. collagen peptides in a supplement, the answer is clear. But you can get the advantages of collagen topically, too. Shop our top picks now.
body: If you’ve ever stood by a shelf or paused mid-scroll to debate the merits of collagen vs. collagen peptides, welcome to the club. Ever since the role of collagen—a key protein in the skin that effectively serves as its scaffolding, keeping it firm and smooth—came to the forefront, it’s become a sought-after ingredient in both topical skin-care products and oral supplements alike. That’s because your own natural stores of collagen break down over time, destroyed by years of sun exposure, sugar consumption, and natural wear-and-tear. It’s understandable, then, that you might want to replace it.

However, re-upping your skin’s natural supply of collagen isn’t quite as simple as ingesting or slathering oneself in more collagen. Here’s what you can do to bolster your skin’s natural stores of the sought-after protein.

articles.title: How Arc’teryx Made Its Most Circular Product Yet
articles.summary: Arc’teryx’s new hardshell jacket is the first fashion product to receive a circularity certification, but combining durability with recyclability is a delicate balance.
body: When Canadian outdoor clothing brand Arc’teryx set out to create its most circular product yet, it drew a hard line in the sand. “We were not interested in creating a product that asked people to accept lower performance in exchange for lower impact,” says VP of advanced concepts Alexandra Plante.

But balancing performance and impact, durability and recyclability, is no small feat. It would take Arc’teryx four years to complete the Sperro SV — a technical hardshell jacket, launching September 4. Plante says it was worth the wait: the Sperro SV is the first fashion product (of any brand globally) to receive the Testex Circularity label, developed by Swiss testing and certification institute Testex to provide a common framework to substantiate circularity.
The Sperro SV is the first product to be released under the brand’s new circularity initiative, System 0, and the first fashion product globally to be certified under the Testex Circularity label.
points: Arc’teryx’s new hardshell jacket is the first fashion product to receive a circularity certification, but combining durability with recyclability is a delicate balance.

articles.title: Meet Vogue’s Global Class of Emerging Designers
articles.summary: To highlight unique voices across the globe, Vogue asked each of the international titles to nominate an emerging designer from their respective region.
body: The best part about working in fashion is discovering the incredibly diverse array of emerging designers out in the world. The way the Taiwanese designer 01 Woomin interprets a suit jacket varies vastly from the ones that Brazil’s Misci makes, but both remain exciting iterations of the classic silhouette. Similarly, it’s always exciting to discover a new batch of disruptors, like Anthony Calydon in Paris. “Self-taught, [Calydon] represents to me a new generation of young French designers building brands directly with their community, in control of their own narrative,” says Claire Thomson-Jonville, head of editorial content at Vogue France.

Design that looks to Brazil rather than drawing inspiration from elsewhere lies at the core of Misci’s philosophy. Reimagined tailoring, defined by body-conscious cutouts and innovative silhouettes, is one of the brand’s signatures. Two materials have become synonymous with Misci: custom-woven jacquards, often featuring hidden tongue-in-cheek phrases, and pirarucu leather, a sustainable alternative made from the skin of the Amazonian pirarucu fish. The label’s handbags are popular and have become instantly recognizable in Brazil.

articles.title: All the Celebrity Sightings at the 2026 U.S. Open
articles.summary: The annual tennis event has turned into an opportunity for stars to step out in their best courtside looks.
body: The 2026 U.S. Open has officially kicked off in Queens, New York City. Just a few days into the annual tournament, we’ve already seen some of the sport’s biggest tennis pros hit the court in style—including world-class players like Serena Williams, Carlos Alcaraz, Novak Djokovic, and Roger Federer.

While much of the excitement will be happening on the court, the event is about more than just the scores: In recent years, the U.S. Open has become a high-profile opportunity for stars to step out in their best courside looks (and flaunt their lucrative brand deals to boot). It’s as much a fashion event as it is a sporting one—just take the latest fashion-forward sightings in the fan stands.

Vogue September cover stars Kaia Gerber and Homer Gere, for one, hit the first week of the U.S. Open in sophisticated outfits. Gerber looked chic in her form-fitting little black dress, while Gere went classic in his blazer, jeans, and crisp white collared shirt. There were even loads of designer sightings amongst the crowd, too: Both Vera Wang and Tory Burch made cameos.
